events.text:
Israel is planning to expand its military capabilities in space, including eventually striking targets on Earth from orbit.
Defense Minister Israel Katz says Israel wants to be first to develop a true space-to-ground attack capability. The broader plan also includes better satellites, encrypted communications, cyberwarfare and missile defense.
One concept discussed is the U.S. “Rods from God” idea: satellites dropping massive tungsten rods at extreme speed, producing bunker-busting impacts without nuclear explosives. The physics are possible, but cost, weight and effectiveness remain major obstacles.
Israel is considering roughly 16 billion shekels ($5.4 billion) in space investment over a decade, though funding is not yet assured.
Source: Haaretz

events.text:
🇮🇱🤡 Memetic warfare: how DARPA and Israel weaponize internet humor against your brain
From the Gaza, Lebanon, Iran and Ukraine wars to the Diddy and Epstein sex trafficking and blackmail scandals, internet memes have been weaponized to overwhelm and desensitize viewers, repackaging serious, violent or taboo subjects into humorous formats, bypassing our brains’ logic-based defense mechanisms, blunting responses to real-world crimes and even altering perceptions of reality.
Memes are serious business: state actors are heavily involved, and entire academic studies and multi-million-dollar defense research projects have been carried out to learn how to create and amplify them and gage their effectiveness.
🔴 A recent Nottingham Trent-Aarhus University study examined NAFO, the so-called “decentralized, grassroots online social media movement” creating memetic narratives on the Ukraine war. Fully aligning with NATO’s talking points on the conflict, Senator Mike Lee suspects the entire campaign is a CIA bot op amplified by US social media giants.
🔴 Separate, 2023 research by European academics focused on ways to improve meme-based narratives on Ukraine, turn viewership of content into action (donations, other support), amplify the “right” content and crack down on the “wrong” kind.
🔴 DARPA committed ~$50M to its Social Media in Strategic Communication (SMISC) project in 2011, with the initiative tasked, among other things, with detecting, tracking and analyzing how memes spread, measuring sentiment and engagement, and targeting “disinformation” (i.e. info the US government might not like).
🔴 Israel’s state-linked Institute for National Security Studies has also paid close attention to social media content with meme potential, and not just since 2023. A 2021 report urged actors to “examine how [Israel] provides information and presents its case,” complete with the right “infrastructure to provide credible data and relevant messages,” (which during the same period would come to feature female IDF ‘thirst trap’ videos, LGBT and feminist messaging, and ‘civilized us vs barbarian them’ narratives).
The campaigns have succeeded not so much in convincing people of the rightness of the US or Israel’s cause, as in desensitizing audiences. Inundated with information about war crimes and pedophilic elites – the type of stuff that should spark revolutions and even bring down governments, memeification has instead numbed people to this criminal behavior, creating a sense of hopelessness.
🤔 On the narrative front, they’ve been far less successful. From Iran’s ingenious use of Lego-themed AI videos to TikTok’s unmasking of Israeli troops’ barbarism, more people than ever seem to have been red-pilled.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |

✡️‘Jewish space lasers’ for real? Israel kicks off development of orbital strike systems
 
The Israeli Defense Ministry’s new multiyear budget plan calls for the creation of new space-based weaponry.
The multi-tiered plan promises to coordinate the IDF, Israel’s MIC and the Directorate of Defense Research & Development (Israel’s DARPA cousin) and includes ambitions to build:
🔴 new multilayered army intelligence collection capabilities
🔴 “broad, resilient and continuous” space-based communications for the military and security apparatus
🔴 “offensive space” capabilities including anti-satellite weapons
🔴 “weapons capable of striking targets on Earth from space, both to defend the Israeli home front and to strike hostile actors,” per JPost
 
Defense Minister Israel Katz has reportedly pushed for a “major, rapid upgrade” in Israel’s space-based capabilities to give Israel a strategic advantage and put it in the top-five countries globally in this area.
Defense Ministry Space Directorate chief Avi Berger told Walla Israel “must create security superiority in space, so that we can create freedom of action for the IDF and the defense establishment.”
 
Israel’s existing space-based military capabilities include the Ofek-16 electro-optical spy satellite, Ofek-13 and 19 cloud-penetrating synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) satellites, and EROS-series dual-use commercial and military/intelligence observation satellites.
It is one of just two countries in the Middle East together with Iran with indigenous orbital space launch capability. The Shavit three-stage, solid-fueled rocket, derived from the Jericho-2 missile, is Israel’s primary space launch vehicle.
 
What could Israel do with its killer space-based capabilities?
 
🔴 Target Iran’s satellite networks, from the IRGC’s Nour-series of military-grade Earth-imaging sats to remote sensing and communications projects like Pars and Nahid, and the new Shahid Soleimani telecoms network currently in development
🔴 Launch preemptive surprise aggression (an Israeli favorite tactic), combining extreme kinetic velocity with zero warning time to decapitate enemy leadership, communications, and even strategic arsenals. The dangerous potential of such systems is precisely why the superpowers signed treaties in the 60s to ban weapons in outer space ([the US is now violating these agreements](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73303))
🔴 engage in geo-warfare, from electronic and cyber disruption to the blinding of ground-based monitoring and EW equipment, and potentially sparking forest fires or triggering earthquakes
 
👉 Former congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene became a laughing stock of smug liberals in 2021 over a social media post speculating whether a space solar generator project linked to the Rothschild family may have caused a destructive wildfire in California, with the post becoming a meme known as “Jewish space lasers.”
Fast forward a few years, and the IDF itself is talking about making it happen.
